subject: Subprocessor consent gap analysis & MSA/Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Katie Smith <katie.smith@stratusai.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@stratusai.com, Greg Barton <greg.barton@gblaw.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed subprocessor (DataBridge Ltd.) + DPA attached — need consent and order form impact

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the product demo last week. We have internal approval to move forward pending a couple of governance items: StratusAI plans to engage a new analytics subprocessor, DataBridge Ltd. (UK/EU), to handle anonymized telemetry and usage metrics tied to the integration.

Attached is our proposed DPA (StratusAI_DPA_Proposed_v1.docx) and a short note from our procurement team on the order-form changes we expect (procurement@stratusai.com copied). Could you confirm:

- Whether Redwood can accept DataBridge as a subprocessor under the current MSA/DPA model, and what specific flow-down clauses you would require?
- If we need to amend the Order Form (scope + pricing) for the subprocessor addition — and if so, an estimate of typical cost/lead time for approval?
- Evidence we can provide (SOC reports, encryption attestations) to speed consent.

We prefer to avoid a full MSA re-execution if possible — a limited order-form amendment and DPA addendum would be ideal. However, counsel (Greg) may have comments on the redlines.

Can we get a preliminary guidance by Friday so our execs can keep the integration timeline?

Thanks,
Katie Smith
Director, Partnerships | StratusAI
T: +1 415 555 0142

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed subprocessor (DataBridge Ltd.) + DPA attached — need consent and order form impact

Katie — thanks for the docs and the heads up. Looping in our Procurement (Priyom) and Legal/Compliance (Kimberly, Connor) to run a quick gap analysis and confirm the approval path.

Quick notes from my side:
- We can typically handle a subprocessor addition with an Order Form addendum + DPA exhibit if the subprocessor's controls meet our baseline (SOC 2 Type II, encryption in transit/at rest, and data residency guarantees where applicable).
- Legal will review the specific flow-down language in your DPA and flag any clauses that would require an MSA-level change (e.g., indemnity carveouts, overly broad audit rights, or permanent data-transfer restrictions).
- Procurement will provide an estimate for any pricing adjustments; sometimes there is a marginal uplift for managed third-party analytics.

Action items:
1) Kimberly/Connor: do a redline pass + highlight clauses that cannot be accepted via a DPA exhibit alone.
2) Priyom: advise on procurement routing and expected cycle time for an Order Form amendment (internal SOW>PO flow).
3) Katie/Greg: please supply recent SOC 2 Type II or equivalent for DataBridge and any subprocessor terms they propose.

We’ll aim to get preliminary guidance by EOD Friday; if legal needs more time we’ll flag a narrower set of negotiation points so we don’t delay the integration.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, katie.smith@stratusai.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, Greg Barton <greg.barton@gblaw.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed subprocessor (DataBridge Ltd.) + DPA attached — need consent and order form impact

Thanks Olga / Katie. I reviewed the attached DPA and pulled a short redline summary (attached: Redline_Summary_MSA-OrderForm_v2.pdf). High level concerns:

1) Flow-down: The DPA attempts to impose full customer-facing audit rights onto the subprocessor. We can accept a right to receive summary SOC/audit reports but cannot permit customer audits of DataBridge without a scoped, pre-approved procedure. Suggest: customer-only review rights via Redwood with escrowed summaries.

2) Indemnity & Liability: The draft broadens StratusAI indemnity for third-party subprocessor claims to include unlimited consequential damages. We need to cap indemnity to what the MSA allows and add carve-outs only for willful misconduct.

3) Data Transfers & Residency: DataBridge is UK-based. We can accept EU processing with standard SCCs, but if Stratus insists on a permanent EU-only residency requirement, that may be an MSA-level change.

4) Notification & Remediation: The DPA asks for immediate notification but provides no SLA. Propose: 72-hour notification for security incidents with a 30-day remediation plan (unless critical data exposure — in that case, 24 hours and emergency escalation).

5) Evidence: Accept SOC 2 Type II reports, encryption attestations, and a security questionnaire (SIG Lite). A signed MSA exhibit + order-form addendum should be sufficient if DataBridge meets the controls.

Procurement note: Priyom, if you can confirm whether pricing uplift is expected and whether we can route this via an order-form amendment (no new MSA), we’ll instruct Katie on the timeline.

Greg — would appreciate you flagging any points you view as non-starters for StratusAI so we can converge quickly.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Contracting & Procurement | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redline_Summary_MSA-OrderForm_v2.pdf
From: Greg Barton <greg.barton@gblaw.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com, katie.smith@stratusai.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed subprocessor (DataBridge Ltd.) + DPA attached — need consent and order form impact

Kimberly / Olga,

Appreciate the quick read. A couple of clarifications from StratusAI counsel:

- Audit rights: Stratus can provide SOC 2 reports and allow Redwood to request supplementary evidence (logs, control matrices) where there is a credible incident. They are reluctant to accept customer-directed on-site audits of DataBridge; we may be able to agree to an independent auditor scope negotiated in advance.

- Indemnity caps: Stratus will not accept unlimited consequential exposure tied to subprocessor acts. They propose a compromise — indemnity limited to direct damages capped at the order-form value for the relevant term, with carve-outs for gross negligence/willful misconduct.

- Notification SLA: Stratus is open to a 72-hour notification window with a 30-day remediation plan for non-critical issues. For security incidents impacting personal data, they propose 48 hours.

We can get DataBridge SOC 2 artifacts over by EOD Thursday. If Redwood can provide a short redline that isolates the three items above (audit, indemnity cap, notification SLA), we can likely resolve with an Order Form amendment + DPA exhibit.

Regards,
Greg Barton
Partner | GB Law LLP
greg.barton@gblaw.com
